summary: No blocking discrepancies. The migrated WinUI 3 app faithfully reproduces the UWP sample across all 4 scenarios, including correct hardware-gated behavior for the device-report scenarios.

discrepancies.scenario: 2-4 (Feature Reports / Input Report Events / Input and Output Reports)
discrepancies.detail: Device-specific controls (Get/Set Led Blink Pattern, Register/Unregister, Send/Get reports, ComboBoxes) are not visible in either the UWP golden or the WinUI candidate because no SuperMUTT HID device is connected. Both apps collapse the SuperMuttScenario panel and show 'Device is not connected, please select a plugged in device to try the scenario again'. This is correct, matching behavior — not a defect.

The original UWP app launched successfully (ground truth confirmed live, PID 64148, window 'Custom HID Device Access C# UAP') and its Scenario 1 was captured. However this .NET Native UWP sample exposes no UIA child tree on this OS, and synthetic input injection to its CoreWindow did not register, so the golden could not be programmatically navigated to scenarios 2-4. Scenario-1 golden was captured and compared visually; scenarios 2-4 were judged against the source-derived rubric and the WinUI UIA tree. No behavioral golden exists because all report scenarios are hardware-gated regardless.

layout_differences.detail: Cosmetic framework differences only: WinUI 3 default light theme vs UWP dark theme, standard title bar. Layout, control placement, and text are faithful to the UWP source.
